mainTopic: How the bird עולה is pinched and where each of its rules comes from; then the right ages for תורין and בני יונה
overview: This עמוד finishes a ברייתא about מליקה, the way a כהן kills a bird קרבן by pinching its neck. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון compares the bird עולה to the bird חטאת: the blood is sprinkled while the head is still attached. The word ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״ shows that the עולה still needs two סימנים cut, not one. The גמרא then explains why the תנא קמא also needs ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״, even though he learns his rule from ״וּמָלַק וְהִקְטִיר״. Next it looks at the rules the תנא קמא learns from the חטאת בהמה. The חולין rule comes from ״אֲשֶׁר לוֹ״. The daytime rule was only listed in passing. The right hand is needed here because the word כהונה alone is not enough. The other תנאים learn the back-of-the-neck rule by comparing the word מליקה in both cases. Then a new משנה teaches that grown תורין and young בני יונה are fit, and the in-between age is unfit for both. Finally, a ברייתא starts to show why the פסוק is needed to rule out young doves. That discussion continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The bird burnt offering is compared to the bird sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's comparison: just as with the bird חטאת the כהן "holds the head and the body and sprinkles," so too with the bird עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Just as there, with the bird sin offering, the priest] holds the head and the body and sprinkles the blood, so too here, with the bird burnt offering, he holds the head and the body and sprinkles.
steps.whatsHappening: We are picking up in the middle of a ברייתא. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון is finishing his comparison between the bird חטאת and the bird עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the comparison is that the bird עולה is done the same way as the bird חטאת. In the חטאת the head is not cut off completely before the blood is sprinkled. So the עולה should also keep its head on when the blood is sprinkled. The exact wording "holds" is unclear, and the גמרא will ask about it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds (the גמרא will soon explain it as "attached")
Sprinkles the blood on the מזבח
"There" (the case we learn from) and "here" (the case we apply it to)
A bird sin offering
A bird burnt offering

steps.confusionAlert: Don't picture the כהן holding the bird in both hands as the main point. The גמרא is about to explain that the real issue is whether the head is still attached to the body.

phrases.english: [just as there, by the bird sin offering] he holds the head and the body and sprinkles,
phrases.notes: "There" is the bird חטאת, from the end of the ברייתא on the previous עמוד.

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן אוֹחֵז בְּרֹאשׁ וּבַגּוּף וּמַזֶּה.
phrases.english: so too here [by the bird burnt offering], he holds the head and the body and sprinkles.

steps.triggerLanguage: אף כאן אוחז בראש ובגוף ומזה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that began on the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bird עולה is done like the bird חטאת: the blood is sprinkled while the head and body are still together.

steps.title: What does "holds the head and the body" mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means, since nobody requires the כהן to hold both the head and the body while sprinkling the blood of a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the ברייתא's wording means. It does not seem to describe any real rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no known requirement that the כהן grip both the head and the body while sprinkling the blood of a bird חטאת. So taking "holds" literally makes the sentence strange. The גמרא wants the real meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? (a request to explain unclear wording)

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the phrase "holds the head and the body and sprinkles" really means.

steps.title: It means the head is still attached to the body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that "אוחז" means "attached." The blood is sprinkled while the head is still attached to the body, in both the חטאת and the עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he is saying: just as there, with the sin offering, he sprinkles while the head is still attached to the body, so too here, with the burnt offering, he sprinkles while the head is still attached to the body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The word means "attached," not "holding."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was not describing how the כהן grips the bird. It was saying that the head is not fully cut off when the blood is sprinkled. That fits רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view that in the עולה you cut most of the two סימנים, not all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (introduces a re-reading of the words)
Attached, connected

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, in the bird עולה the head stays attached to the body when the blood is sprinkled, just as in the bird חטאת.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן, כְּשֶׁהוּא אָחוּז הָרֹאשׁ בַּגּוּף מַזֶּה,
phrases.english: Just as there, when the head is attached to the body, he sprinkles,
phrases.notes: Same root as אוחז, but here read it as "attached," not "holding."

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן, כְּשֶׁהוּא אָחוּז הָרֹאשׁ בַּגּוּף מַזֶּה.
phrases.english: so too here, when the head is attached to the body, he sprinkles.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "אוחז" means the head is attached to the body when the blood is sprinkled.

steps.title: Should the burnt offering need only one סימן, like the sin offering?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges its own comparison: if the עולה is like the חטאת, maybe it also needs only one סימן cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then just as there the sin offering is done with one סימן, perhaps here too the burnt offering is done with one סימן?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a problem with its own comparison. If we compare the עולה to the חטאת, maybe we should copy all of the חטאת's rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bird חטאת needs only one סימן cut. If the עולה is learned from the חטאת for keeping the head attached, we might think it also needs only one סימן. That would go too far.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, just as... (pushes a comparison further to test it)
One of the two organs cut in slaughter: the windpipe or the food pipe

phrases.english: If just as there [it is done] with one siman,
so too here with one siman?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the comparison from steps 1 and 3 by pushing it further.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of the bird עולה to the bird חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison works for keeping the head attached, it should also mean only one סימן is needed.

steps.title: The word "and he shall bring it" shows the burnt offering is different
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the פסוק ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״: the עולה is done differently from the חטאת and needs two סימנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "And he shall bring it."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge with a word from the פסוק. It limits the comparison so that it does not include the one-סימן rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״ teaches that the עולה is offered in its own way, with two סימנים cut. So the comparison to the חטאת covers only keeping the head attached, not the number of סימנים.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse comes to teach (introduces a פסוק that settles the question)
"And he shall bring it" (ויקרא א:טו)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: the עולה keeps its head attached like the חטאת, but it needs two סימנים, learned from ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״.

phrases.english: The verse states: "And he shall bring it."

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עולה might need only one סימן, like the חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״ shows the עולה needs two סימנים.

steps.title: What does the first opinion do with "and he shall bring it"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the תנא קמא already learned his rule from ״וּמָלַק … וְהִקְטִיר״, so why does he need the word ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״?
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for the תנא קמא: since we already learn the rule from "and pinch off… and burn it," why do I need "and he shall bring it"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side of the argument, the תנא קמא. It asks what purpose the word ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״ serves for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the תנא קמא learned from putting ״וּמָלַק״ next to ״וְהִקְטִיר״ that both סימנים of the bird עולה are fully cut. If his rule already comes from there, the word ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״ seems to have no job. The גמרא will need to find one for it.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the ברייתא
We derive it (from a certain source)
"And pinch off… and burn it" (ויקרא א:טו)
Why do I need it? (asks what an extra word is for)

phrases.english: And the first tanna,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּנָפְקָא לַן מִ״וּמָלַק … וְהִקְטִיר״,
phrases.english: since we derive it from "and pinch off… and burn it,"
phrases.notes: This is the תנא קמא's source from the previous עמוד. Both words are in ויקרא א:טו.

phrases.english: why do I need "and he shall bring it"?

steps.triggerLanguage: ותנא קמא וכי מאחר דנפקא לן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After seeing how רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון uses ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״, the גמרא asks how the תנא קמא uses it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's way of reading the פסוקים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the תנא קמא gets his rule from ״וּמָלַק … וְהִקְטִיר״, the word ״וְהִקרִיבוֹ״ seems to be extra for him.

steps.title: Without this word we would misread 'according to the rule'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״ is needed. Without it, ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״ could mean the עולה follows the rules of the חטאת העוף. And ״וּמָלַק וְהִקְטִיר״ would only teach that the pinching happens on top of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not for the word ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״, I would have said: what does ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״ ('according to the rule') mean? It means according to the rule of the חטאת העוף. And if you say ״וּמָלַק וְהִקְטִיר״ already rules that out, I would have said that phrase teaches something else: just as the burning is on top of the מזבח, so too the pinching is on top of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 6. It shows that without ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״ we could have reached the wrong rule, because ״וּמָלַק וְהִקְטִיר״ would have been used to teach something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״ by the עולת העוף could be read as 'like the חטאת העוף mentioned right before it.' That would mean only one סימן is cut. We cannot rely on ״וּמָלַק וְהִקְטִיר״ to stop this mistake, because we would have used it for a different lesson: the place of the מליקה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'According to the rule'. A word in the פסוק about the עולת העוף.
A bird brought as a חטאת. Only one סימן is cut, and the head is not fully removed.
'I would have said'. This introduces a mistaken first thought.
Burning the offering on the מזבח.
Pinching: the כהן's fingernail cut on a bird's neck.
The top of the מזבח.

steps.confusionAlert: There are three different sources here. ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״ teaches that the עולה is different from the חטאת. ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״ is the word that could have misled us. ״וּמָלַק וְהִקְטִיר״ is the phrase the תנא קמא used. Keep them apart.

phrases.english: If not for "and he shall bring it,"
I would have said:
What does "according to the rule" mean?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:10, about the bird עולה brought together with a bird חטאת.

phrases.english: According to the rule of the bird sin offering.
And if you say this is ruled out because of "and he shall pinch and burn",
I would have said:
Just as the burning is on top of the altar,
so too the pinching is on top of the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6's question about why ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״ is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that each source is needed by giving another use for ״וּמָלַק וְהִקְטִיר״.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״ means the עולה is done like the חטאת העוף, with one סימן. ״וּמָלַק וְהִקְטִיר״ only teaches where the pinching is done.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״ is needed to teach that the עולה is different and needs two סימנים.

steps.title: Now the pinch-and-burn phrase can teach this too
steps.stepSummary: Since the תורה wrote ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״ to show the difference, ״וּמָלַק וְהִקְטִיר״ can also be used to teach this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that the תורה wrote ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״, you can also learn this from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up its answer. ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״ takes care of the mistaken reading, so ״וּמָלַק וְהִקְטִיר״ is free to teach this rule as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that ״וּמָלַק וְהִקְטִיר״ would be 'used up' teaching where the pinching happens. Once ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״ blocks the idea that the עולה is like the חטאת, ״וּמָלַק וְהִקְטִיר״ can also teach this. That is the full separation of head and body that the תנא קמא learned from it. So both sources have a job.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One', meaning the תורה or ה׳.
Learn out, expound.

steps.whatToRemember: Each source has its own job. ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״ shows that the עולת העוף is different from the חטאת העוף. ״וּמָלַק וְהִקְטִיר״ can then teach this as well.

phrases.english: Now that the Merciful One wrote "and he shall bring it,"
learn this also from it.
phrases.notes: "It" is ״וּמָלַק וְהִקְטִיר״, which can now also teach that the head comes fully off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer begun in Step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״ teaches that the עולה is different. ״וּמָלַק וְהִקְטִיר״ can also teach this rule.

steps.title: Where do we learn that an animal sin offering comes only from unconsecrated property?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a חטאת בהמה may only come from חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal חטאת may only come from חולין. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new point. The ברייתא compared the עולת העוף to the חטאת בהמה, so now the גמרא asks where the חטאת בהמה rule itself comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא learned some rules for the עולת העוף from the חטאת בהמה. One rule is that it may only be brought from חולין, not from מעשר שני money. That only works if we have a source for this rule by the חטאת בהמה. The גמרא now looks for that source.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal (not a bird) brought as a חטאת.
Ordinary, unconsecrated property.
'From where do we know?' A request for a source.

phrases.english: An animal sin offering,
which comes only from unconsecrated property,
from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״ discussion and asks about another detail of the ברייתא's comparison.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches a חטאת בהמה may only come from חולין.

steps.title: His own bull: not communal, not tithe money
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא brings the source from the פסוק about אהרן's bull. It must be 'his own', so it cannot be community property or bought with מעשר money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: the פסוק says, 'And אהרן shall bring the bull of the חטאת that is his.' This means from his own, not from the community's and not from מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers Step 9 with a פסוק. The words 'that is his' teach that the animal must belong to the owner himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'that is his' look extra, so they teach a rule. The animal cannot come from the community's funds. It also cannot come from מעשר שני money, since that money is not fully his to spend on anything he wants. This gives us the חולין rule for a חטאת בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull brought as a חטאת by the כהן גדול on יום כיפור.
The community.
Here this means מעשר שני property or money.

steps.whatToRemember: ״אֲשֶׁר לוֹ״, 'that is his', teaches that a חטאת בהמה must come from the owner's own חולין. It cannot come from community funds or from מעשר.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said,
for the verse says:
"And Aaron shall bring
the bull of the sin offering that is his,"
from his own, and not from the community's,
and not from tithe property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source asked for in Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From ״אֲשֶׁר לוֹ״ in ויקרא 16: the animal must be his own, not the community's and not from מעשר.

steps.title: Daytime already has its own source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: why learn that the עולת העוף is brought by day from the חטאת בהמה, when ״בְּיוֹם צַוֹּתוֹ״ already teaches it?
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule that it must be done during the day already comes from the פסוק ״בְּיוֹם צַוֹּתוֹ״!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges one item in the ברייתא's list. The daytime rule already has its own פסוק, so it should not need to be learned from the חטאת בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא listed ״by day″ as something we learn from the חטאת בהמה through ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״. But ״בְּיוֹם צַוֹּתוֹ״ already teaches that all קרבנות are brought by day. So putting it in this list looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: "On the day He commanded". The פסוק that teaches קרבנות are brought by day.
It comes out from / it is learned from

phrases.english: During the day —
that is already learned from "on the day He commanded"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's list of rules learned from the חטאת בהמה and checks each item.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the daytime rule comes from the חטאת בהמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule already has its own direct פסוק (״בְּיוֹם צַוֹּתוֹ״), so learning it from the חטאת בהמה would be extra.

steps.title: Daytime was listed just in passing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תנא mentioned ״by day″ only in passing. It is not really learned from here.
steps.simpleTranslation: He just mentioned it for no special reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The daytime rule was listed along with the others, but nothing is actually being learned from it here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer agrees that ״בְּיוֹם צַוֹּתוֹ״ is the real source. The ברייתא included ״by day″ only because it was describing how the חטאת בהמה is done. This leaves the other items in the list as real learnings.

keyTerms.meaning: He brought it for nothing. It was mentioned in passing.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא is wrong about the daytime rule. The rule is true. It just comes from a different פסוק.

phrases.english: He cited it for no special reason.
phrases.notes: He means it was just listed together with the other rules. It is not really being learned from ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Agrees there is another source and explains that the item was only mentioned in passing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The daytime rule is learned from the חטאת בהמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The daytime rule comes from ״בְּיוֹם צַוֹּתוֹ״. The ברייתא only mentioned it along the way.

steps.title: The right hand already has its own source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the right-hand item. It seems to come from ריש לקיש's rule that wherever ״אצבע″ or ״כהונה״ is written, the right hand is meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: The right hand rule already comes from רבה בר בר חנה, who said in the name of ריש לקיש: wherever the תורה says 'finger' or 'priesthood', it means the right hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges another item in the list. The right-hand rule seems to have its own source, ריש לקיש's general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים of the עולת העוף mention the כהן. By ריש לקיש's rule, that alone should require the right hand. So why does the ברייתא need ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״ to teach it?

keyTerms.meaning: Finger
Priesthood. The word כהן written in the פסוק.
The right hand

steps.whyThisMatters: ריש לקיש's rule is the main general source for doing the עבודה with the right hand.

phrases.english: His right hand —
that is learned from the teaching of Rabbah bar bar Chana,
as Rabbah bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אֶצְבַּע אוֹ כְהוּנָּה
phrases.english: Any place where "finger" or "priesthood" is said,
it means only the right hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָדוֹ הַיְמָנִית מִדְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of challenge as step 11, now aimed at the right-hand item.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the right-hand rule comes from the חטאת בהמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש's general rule already requires the right hand whenever כהונה is mentioned, and the עולת העוף mentions the כהן.

steps.title: The word כהונה alone is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא holds that ״כהונה״ only requires the right hand when ״אצבע״ is also written. ״אצבע״ works even by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other תנא holds: 'priesthood' needs 'finger' with it, but 'finger' does not need 'priesthood'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תנא קמא reads ריש לקיש's rule more narrowly. The word ״כהונה״ alone does not prove the right hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the עולת העוף, only the word כהן appears. The word אצבע does not. So for the תנא קמא, ריש לקיש's rule does not cover this case, and he needs ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״ to teach the right hand.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one. Here, the תנא קמא of the ברייתא.
Needs / requires

steps.whatToRemember: For the תנא קמא, ״אצבע״ alone requires the right hand, but ״כהונה״ alone does not. That is why he needs ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״ for the עולת העוף.

phrases.english: And the other one (the first Tanna) holds:
"priesthood" needs "finger" together with it,
but "finger" does not need "priesthood".

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the scope of the general rule so it does not cover this case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any mention of כהונה alone requires the right hand, so ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״ is not needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: כהונה requires the right hand only together with אצבע. So for the עולת העוף, the right hand must be learned from the חטאת בהמה.

steps.title: Where do the others learn the back-of-the-neck rule?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל learned ממול העורף from ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״. The תנא קמא and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון used that word for other things, so where do they learn it from?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא קמא and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, from where do they know that the pinching is done opposite the back of the neck?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of a rule according to the תנאים who used ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״ for something else. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי ישמעאל used ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״ to teach that the עולת העוף is pinched at the back of the neck, like a חטאת העוף. The other two תנאים used that word for different rules. So they need another source for this one.

keyTerms.meaning: Opposite the back of the neck. The place where the מליקה is done.
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
From where do they know it?

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: And the first Tanna and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,
from where do they know "opposite the back of the neck"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מִמּוּל הָעוֹרֶף מְנָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the list of rules learned from the חטאת בהמה to רבי ישמעאל's rule about where the bird is pinched.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for pinching the עולת העוף at the back of the neck, according to the תנאים who did not use ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״ for it.

steps.title: They learn pinching from pinching
steps.stepSummary: They learn from the shared word מליקה. Since the חטאת העוף is pinched at the back of the neck, the עולת העוף is too.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn 'pinching' written by the עולה from 'pinching' written by the חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these תנאים compare the word ״מליקה״ in both פסוקים. That comparison teaches the back-of-the-neck rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of the חטאת העוף says the pinching is ״מִמּוּל עָרְפּוֹ״, by the back of the neck. The עולת העוף also uses the word מליקה, so the same detail carries over. This way they do not need ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״ for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Pinching. Killing a bird קרבן by cutting with the כהן's fingernail.
They learn (one case from another)

steps.whatToRemember: All the תנאים agree the עולת העוף is pinched at the back of the neck. They only disagree about the source: ״כַּמִּשְׁפָּט״ or the shared word מליקה.

phrases.english: They learn "pinching" from "pinching".
phrases.notes: The עולה's pinching is in ויקרא 1:15, and the חטאת's pinching, ״מִמּוּל עָרְפּוֹ״, is in ויקרא 5:8.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They learn the rule by comparing the word מליקה written by the עולת העוף with the same word written by the חטאת העוף.

steps.title: The age that is fit for one kind of bird is unfit for the other
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the right age for תורין is the wrong age for בני יונה, and the reverse. The in-between stage is unfit for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The age that is fit for תורין (doves) is unfit for בני יונה (young pigeons). The age that is fit for בני יונה is unfit for תורין. When the feathers just start turning yellow, the bird is unfit as either one.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts a new topic. It teaches which ages of birds may be brought as a bird קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה lets a person bring two kinds of birds, תורין and בני יונה, and each kind has its own right age. The age that makes one kind fit makes the other kind unfit. There is also a middle stage, the start of the yellowing of the feathers, when the bird is unfit as either kind.

keyTerms.meaning: Doves (turtledoves). This kind of bird is fit for a קרבן when it is grown up.
Young pigeons. This kind of bird is fit for a קרבן when it is young.
Fit, allowed to be brought as a קרבן
Unfit, not allowed to be brought as a קרבן
The beginning of the yellowing of the feathers. This is the in-between age.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think one kind of bird is simply better than the other. Each kind has its own right age, and the two rules are opposites.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ כָּשֵׁר בְּתוֹרִין – פָּסוּל בִּבְנֵי יוֹנָה,
phrases.english: MISHNA: What is fit in doves is unfit in young pigeons,
what is fit in young pigeons is unfit in doves,
the beginning of the yellowing, in this one and in that one, is unfit.
phrases.notes: That's the in-between age, no longer a baby but not yet grown, so the bird can't be brought as either kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic. It moves on from the discussion of מליקה to the right ages of birds for a קרבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The age that makes תורין fit makes בני יונה unfit, and the reverse. The start of yellowing makes a bird unfit as either kind.

steps.title: A ברייתא spells out the ages: grown doves, young pigeons
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains the משנה: grown תורין are fit and young ones are unfit. Young בני יונה are fit and grown ones are unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Grown תורין are fit and young ones are unfit. Young בני יונה are fit and grown ones are unfit. So what is fit in תורין is unfit in בני יונה, and what is fit in בני יונה is unfit in תורין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the משנה. It tells us exactly which age is fit for each kind of bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said the fit age of one kind is the unfit age of the other, without saying which age is which. The ברייתא fills that in: תורין must be big and בני יונה must be small. Then it shows how this leads straight to the משנה's wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Big, grown-up birds
Small, young birds
It turns out, so the result is

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
Doves that are big are fit, small ones are unfit;

phrases.aramaic: בְּנֵי יוֹנָה קְטַנִּים – כְּשֵׁרִים, גְּדוֹלִים – פְּסוּלִין.
phrases.english: young pigeons that are small are fit, big ones are unfit.

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא כָּשֵׁר בְּתוֹרִין – פָּסוּל בִּבְנֵי יוֹנָה,
phrases.english: It turns out that what is fit in doves is unfit in young pigeons,
and what is fit in young pigeons is unfit in doves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה by saying which age is fit for each kind of bird.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grown תורין and young בני יונה are fit. Young תורין and grown בני יונה are unfit.
steps.whatToRemember: תורין must be big and בני יונה must be small. This is why the fit age of one is the unfit age of the other.

steps.title: A ברייתא starts to show that only grown doves are fit
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא learns from the word תורים that the doves must be grown and not young. It then begins asking whether logic alone could have taught this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "תורים" means grown ones and not young ones. You might have thought: couldn't this be worked out by logic?
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא learns the rule for תורין from the פסוק. It then starts setting up a logical argument, which the next part of the גמרא will develop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the word תורים in the פסוק teaches that only grown doves are fit. It explains why the פסוק is needed: without it, one might have thought (״שֶׁיָּכוֹל״) that a logical argument, a דין, leads the other way, so that young doves would be fit too. The words "שיכול והלא דין הוא" only open that mistaken argument; the argument and the reply come on the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: "You might have thought." It introduces an idea that will be looked at and usually rejected.
"Isn't it a matter of logic?" It introduces an attempt to prove a rule by reasoning, often a קל וחומר.

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא has not finished its point here. "והלא דין הוא" opens a logical argument that would have reached the wrong rule (young doves are fit). The argument and its rejection come on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: "Doves"
means big ones and not small ones,
for one might have thought: but isn't it a matter of logic?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from stating the rule to finding where it comes from in the פסוק. It begins by raising whether logic alone could teach it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word תורים teaches that only grown doves are fit, not young ones.
